item.title: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses
item.description: arXiv:2611.13032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Caustics provide a universal connection between classical ray focusing and structured wave patterns. We theoretically investigate this connection in non-linear matter waves focused by a short-duration anharmonic lens acting on a Bose-Einstein condensate. A semi-classical description shows how the leading cubic aberration transforms the harmonic focal point into a fold caustic, whose local wave field is described by an Airy canonical integral. Three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that mean-field interactions modify the near-focus density and longitudinal momentum distribution, producing a secondary momentum-space feature absent from the non-interacting evolution. We quantify the information about the effective interaction strength carried by the $1D$ distribution using classical Fisher information and maximum-likelihood estimation. We obtain a relative uncertainty of $2.7\times10^{-3}$ for a sample of $10^5$ detected points along $z$. These results establish a framework for studying interaction-driven departures from single-particle caustic universality and promote matter-wave lenses as a sensitive probe of mean-field interactions.
item.dc:creator: Joachim Guyomard, Julia Pahl, Ernst Rasel, Naceur Gaaloul

item.title: Pair localization in one-dimensional quasicrystals with spin-dependent hopping
item.description: arXiv:2611.13553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the quantum localization of two interacting particles moving in a one-dimensional quasicrystal with unequal hopping amplitudes. Using a two-body Green's function approach, we determine the localization phase diagram of attractively and repulsively bound pairs, showing that increasing the hopping amplitude of one constituent while keeping the other fixed raises the critical quasiperiodic strength, promoting pair delocalization. The localization threshold nevertheless remains bounded above by the Aubry-Andr\'e critical point of the slower constituent. Effective analytical descriptions capture pair localization in the limits of strong hopping imbalance and strong interactions. The dynamics of an initially on-site pair provides signatures of delocalization induced by unequal hopping amplitudes. In particular, the effective spreading exponent of the root-mean-square width of a pair distribution reveals a progression from localized to subdiffusive and eventually superdiffusive behavior as the hopping ratio increases. Our results establish unequal hopping amplitudes as a means of tuning the transport properties of interacting pairs in quasiperiodic lattices, with direct relevance to ultracold atoms in optical lattices.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Rosas, U. A. D\'iaz-Reynoso, Francisco Mireles, G. A. Dom\'inguez-Castro

item.title: Nonreciprocal Josephson Dynamics of a $\mathcal{PT}$-Symmetric Atomtronic SQUID
item.description: arXiv:2611.14291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate non-Hermitian Josephson dynamics in an atomtronic quantum interference device (AQUID), formed by a ring Bose Einstein condensate with balanced atomic gain and loss regions and two moving optical barriers. The balanced gain and loss profile establishes a parity time symmetric potential while breaking spatial inversion symmetry, providing the essential ingredients for nonreciprocal Josephson transport. The dynamics are monitored nondestructively through the phase quadrature spectrum of an optomechanical cavity driven by Laguerre Gaussian beams coupled to the condensate. We demonstrate that increasing the local gain and loss strength softens the parity time symmetric collective mode towards an exceptional point, as verified by Bogoliubov de Gennes analysis. The associated coherent population exchange produces an additional characteristic splitting in the cavity output spectrum. For linearly translating barriers, non-Hermiticity provides an additional control parameter for tuning the critical current. When the barriers undergo simultaneous translation and rotation, the rotation induced phase modifies the interference between counter propagating currents, offering further control over the nonreciprocal response. Under periodic barrier modulation, we find more pronounced Shapiro steps in the current voltage characteristics due to the intrinsic parity time symmetric collective mode. Finally, we propose an alternative Hermitian realization using a tilted optical lattice, providing an experimentally accessible route to engineering biased transport and population transfer. Our results establish parity time symmetric atomtronic SQUIDs as a versatile platform for controlling nonreciprocal Josephson transport and collective excitations in driven quantum fluids.
item.dc:creator: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, Pankaj K. Mishra

item.title: Neutron Scattering studies of the density dependence of One-dimensional Quantum Fluids
item.description: arXiv:2611.13235v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In previous work, we demonstrated that $^4$He confined within a templated porous material preplated with a noble gas to enhance dimensional reduction exhibits one-dimensional behavior. Neutron scattering revealed that the excitations in confined $^4$He are qualitatively distinct from those in two- and three-dimensional superfluid helium, aligning with quantum Monte Carlo calculations. These simulations suggest that three solid layers form, with a one-dimensional liquid located at the center of the pore. Here, we present neutron scattering results as the filling fraction of the one-dimensional core is varied. We observe that the one-dimensional liquid always forms with a fixed density, even as the pore filling increases. We posit that this is due to the growth of the one dimensional extent of the liquid as the filling is increased, but its density remains unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Sutirtha Paul, Rahul Soni, Garfield Warren, Adrian Del Maestro, Paul E. Sokol

item.title: Inverse Scattering & Isospectrality in (Analog) Cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2611.13871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cosmological particle production, the excitation of field quanta by a dynamical spacetime, underlies the primordial perturbations observed in the cosmic microwave background and has been realized in analog quantum simulators with ultra-cold atoms. We ask the inverse question: given the excitation spectrum, can the cosmological history that produced it be reconstructed, and is that reconstruction unique? We approach this problem through a mapping of particle production to one-dimensional quantum scattering, in which the expansion history plays the role of a scattering landscape and the produced spectrum the role of reflected and transmitted waves. This mapping reveals a rich interplay between scattering theory and cosmology. The scale factor enters as a zero-energy resonance, an exceptional case of scattering theory, while cosmic singularities correspond to bound states, so that regular cosmologies are governed entirely by the scattering continuum. We find an interesting isospectrality: histories related by an inversion of the scale factor (expansion <-> contraction) yield identical particle numbers, differing only by a pi-shift in phase. Given both the particle number (or alternatively the amplitude) and phase of the cosmological power spectrum, the reconstruction is unique for regular, asymptotically static cosmologies. We demonstrate the reconstruction both analytically, for exactly solvable scattering landscapes, and numerically, recovering common logistic expansion histories to better than 0.02%. We further quantify its robustness to the momentum-space resolution and measurement uncertainties characteristic of analog quantum simulation. This work establishes a direct link between the observable power spectrum and the cosmological history that produced it, offering a new perspective on the classification of early-universe scenarios and the construction of alternatives to inflation.
item.dc:creator: Christian F. Schmidt, Stefan Floerchinger

item.title: Disorder-Induced Logarithmic Spreading and Localization of Quantum Fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Disorder can localize quantum particles, even in the presence of interactions, but its influence on quantum fluctuations beyond mean--field dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the propagation of quantum fluctuations in weakly interacting disordered bosonic systems by comparing the Bose--Hubbard model with the Gross--Pitaevskii equation. We find that, in contrast to ballistic spreading in the disorder--free system, quantum fluctuations exhibit logarithmic spreading at intermediate times under both random and quasiperiodic disorder, before eventually saturating. The spreading rate decreases algebraically with increasing disorder strength, and this behavior persists across different particle numbers and extends to two dimensions. Using a time--dependent Bogoliubov--de Gennes framework, we identify the localized mean--field wavefunction as a time--dependent pairing background that generates quantum fluctuations. The exponential suppression of fluctuation--generation rates with distance provides a physical mechanism for the logarithmically advancing fluctuation front. Our results reveal a distinct regime of disorder--controlled quantum--fluctuation dynamics and establish disorder as a means of controlling their spreading.
item.dc:creator: Ang Yang, Jingxuan Zhang, Lei Ying

item.title: Quantum fields in a cold atomic simulator: relaxation and phase locking in tunnel-coupled 1D bosonic quasi-condensates
item.description: arXiv:2512.13901v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a prime example of simulating interacting relativistic QFT with cold atoms: the realisation of the sine-Gordon model by tunnel-coupled quasi-1D Bose gases. While experiments have shown that it can realise the sine-Gordon model in equilibrium, studies of non-equilibrium dynamics have revealed phase-locking behaviour that contrasts with predictions from sine-Gordon field theory. Here, we examine a one-dimensional field-theoretic model of the system and find that the phase-locking behaviour can be understood in terms of the longitudinal harmonic trap, and that the additional degrees of freedom observed in the experiment do not appear to play a significant role. Therefore, the experimental setup provides a good simulator of the sine-Gordon quantum field theory, even out of equilibrium, if the inhomogeneous background induced by the trap is taken into account. Furthermore, our results support the idea that modifying the longitudinal trap to a box shape should result in agreement with standard sine-Gordon dynamics. The main remaining open issues are accounting for 3D corrections and modelling the effect of the boundaries.
item.dc:creator: B. Fitos, G. Tak\'acs

item.title: Fermi gas of polar molecules in the Pauli-blocked regime
item.description: arXiv:2606.14135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum gases of polar molecules have recently emerged as a powerful platform for exploring exotic many-body dynamics and correlated quantum behavior. To achieve the full potential of this platform, the production of deeply degenerate quantum gases of molecules in arbitrary confinement geometries is necessary. Here, we successfully evaporate fermionic KRb molecules in both 3D and quasi-2D geometries to well below their Fermi temperatures utilizing dipolar collisions. As we evaporate deeper into degeneracy in both geometries, we enter the Pauli-blocked regime with polar molecules, which we independently confirm by measuring the Pauli suppression of elastic collisions. Moreover, the Pauli suppression of collisions contributes to the limitation of our final molecular temperature to about 25% of the Fermi temperature in both geometries, particularly limiting quasi-2D evaporation where the Pauli blockade drastically reduces an otherwise large elastic to inelastic scattering ratio. This work demonstrates the production of degenerate Fermi gases of polar molecules both in a 3D harmonic trap and in mono- and bi-layer 2D configurations. Further, our work explores the fundamental limits on evaporation of molecular Fermi gases set by the Pauli-exclusion principle, which could be overcome in the future by introducing distinguishable scattering partners.
item.dc:creator: Junyu Lin, Annette N. Carroll, Phillip Martin, Calder Miller, Reuben R. W. Wang, Kevin B. Xu, John L. Bohn, Tim de Jongh, Jun Ye

item.title: Quantum droplets and condensates in an optical lattice coupled to a dissipative cavity: Collective excitations and non-equilibrium dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2606.24580v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by recent experiments on light-matter interacting systems, we investigate a dilute Bose gas and self-bound quantum droplets in a one-dimensional optical lattice coupled to a lossy cavity mode. Using a classical-field approach, we determine the stationary states and collective excitations of this non-equilibrium system. Apart from the usual Bogoliubov modes, we identify a polariton-like gapped excitation, the frequency of which softens as a precursor of the density ordering transition. Moreover, its relaxation time diverges as the critical point is approached, signaling the non-equilibrium nature of this transition. Dynamically, this polariton-like mode can be probed by inducing cavity field fluctuations, which in turn generates spatio-temporal oscillations of both the condensate and droplet states. In the droplet regime, we also analyze the bound modes which bear the characteristics of such non-equilibrium self-bound state. In addition, we uncover solitonic non-equilibrium states, including condensate with kink-like configuration and double-droplet state, and investigate their robustness following a sudden quench. Remarkably, although these states become unstable beyond a critical coupling, they continue to manifest in the dynamics, akin to the scarring phenomena. Our results demonstrate that dissipative cavity coupling provides a versatile route for exploring rich non-equilibrium dynamics of condensates and quantum droplets within experimentally accessible settings.
item.dc:creator: G. Vivek, Sudip Sinha, Subhasis Sinha

item.title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.04015v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an interaction-driven route to Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial noninteracting bands in a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and an attractive Hubbard interaction. The large Zeeman splitting renders the noninteracting bands topologically trivial and suppresses spin-flip hopping. These otherwise off-resonant spin-flip processes are resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, generating occupation-dependent spin-orbit coupling that coherently couples neighboring spin-down fermion pairs to onsite doublons. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. A self-consistent mean-field treatment of the microscopic model yields Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, together with fully gapped weak topological superfluids. Tuning the interaction strength and particle filling drives transitions between these phases and controls the number of Weyl nodes. We further propose an experimental implementation with ultracold ${}^{40}\mathrm{K}$ atoms. Our results provide a route to Weyl superfluidity enabled by interaction-assisted spin-orbit coupling, without requiring nontrivial single-particle band topology.
item.dc:creator: Yong-Huan Wang, Xin-Chi Zhou

item.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.09855v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions. Numerically, we show that the dressed gas displays the defining properties of 1D anyons, namely a density-dependent asymmetry of the ground-state momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport and chiral bound states. Remarkably, these features are readily accessible with Raman-coupled $^{39}$K atoms, opening up the experimental exploration of 1D anyons beyond the few-particle regime.
item.dc:creator: Josep Cabedo, Claudio Iacovelli, Leticia Tarruell, Alessio Celi

item.title: Spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry at a non-conformal quantum critical point in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2511.09097v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we present numerical evidence for the spontaneous breaking of a continuous $U(1)$ symmetry in a nearest-neighbor interacting spin-1 chain at a quantum critical point separating two XY quasi-long-range ordered phases distinguished by a spontaneously broken $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. Remarkably, the continuous symmetry breaking emerges precisely at the critical point of the discrete order parameter, suggesting a novel mechanism beyond currently established scenarios. At criticality, the XY correlations develop true long-range order, accompanied by a finite perpendicular magnetization, a zero-frequency Bragg peak in the transverse dynamical structure factor, and sharp gapless collective excitations. From complementary static and dynamical observables, we quantitatively determine the critical exponents, obtaining a dynamical exponent $z=1.50\pm0.04$ and an anomalous dimension $\eta=1.04\pm0.03$. We further show that the non-interacting continuum limit is equivalent to the recently introduced transverse quantum fluid, displaying their off-diagonal long-ranged order in one dimension. Complementing the numerical study, we derive the renormalization-group flow equations of the continuum theory to second order in the $\varepsilon$ expansion. We identify an interacting fixed point whose critical behavior differs from the Ising universality class already at two-loop order, although the perturbative exponents remain far from the numerical values.
item.dc:creator: R. Flores-Calder\'on, M. Z\"undel

item.title: Heisenberg-Langevin theory of an exciton mirror
item.description: arXiv:2606.12053v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a Heisenberg-Langevin theory of an exciton mirror accounting for the retardation and the long-range electron-hole exchange. The particular case of a single-component exciton gas is analyzed in detail. The optical bistability due to repulsion between the excitons inside the light cone appears to be prone to a modulational instability towards the non-radiative polariton modes. Above the corresponding threshold, the pumped 2D exciton gas acts as an optical parametric generator of twin polariton beams. Conversely, below the threshold, the mirror acquires the phase-conjugating properties.
item.dc:creator: Sergue\"i V. Andreev
